thread:
Jordan: heads up — saw a ~20% increase in 95p tail on the inference pool after last night's microbatch/jitter change. cc @Maria @Lee :eyes:
Maria: thanks. which change specifically? the deploy notes mention coalesce_jitter bumped to 1.0 and microbatch_interval nudged to 8ms?
Jordan: yep. deploy log snippet: `coalesce_jitter=1.0, microbatch_interval_ms=8, coalesce_delay_ms=2`
perf-bot: Automated alert: 95th latency delta +19% vs baseline (last 24h). KV cache miss rate +3.1%. Top hotspots: kernel fallback path, kernel selection thrash.
Lee: hmm. early hypothesis: larger jitter increases variance in batch sizes -> more partial batches -> more cache churn and more kernel variant switching. have profiler traces?
Jordan: attaching top stack sample (summarized):
```
samples: 1200
- fused_attn_v2 (happy path) 44%
- fallback_generic_attention 33%  <-- increased from 18% baseline
- kv_cache_lookup 12%
- kernel_dispatch_overhead 7%  <-- up ~0.5ms
```
Maria: fallback_generic is heavier on kernel init and tends to force memory syncs. If we see fallback % up that's consistent with the latency bump. Can you repro with traffic replay?
Jordan: running a 15m replay now with our arrival emulator. command: `scripts/replay_arrival.py --trace recent_peak.json --jitter=1.0 --micro-ms=8`
Lee: while that runs, we should check two signals: per-token kernel selection log and per-worker KV eviction rate. `kubectl logs -f runtime-worker | grep kernel_select` and `metrics: kv_evictions_total`
Jordan: replay done. quick numbers:
- baseline (jitter=0.3, micro=4ms): 95p=48ms, kv_miss=4.2%
- current (jitter=1.0, micro=8ms): 95p=57ms, kv_miss=7.3%
Maria: that's significant. miss delta +3.1% matches prod alert. That extra miss drives re-materializing KV buckets and forces some kernel variants when cache layout changes.
Lee: two experiments to isolate:
1) Pin kernel selection to fused_attn_v2 to see latency delta (disable fallback).
2) Reduce jitter to 0.2 but keep microbatch_interval at 8ms to see whether jitter is the main lever.
Jordan: I pinned kernel selection in a local build and re-ran the replay: 95p dropped to 50ms, kv_miss unchanged. So kernel fallback contributes ~7ms tail.
Maria: interesting — KV miss rate unchanged when pinning kernel suggests eviction is upstream (batch formation) not kernel decision. Maybe larger microbatch interval + jitter patterns cause colder KV hotspots.
Lee: idea: adjust coalesce_delay_ms to 1 and set jitter to a bounded distribution (triangular) instead of exponential to reduce outlier waits. Might reduce partial batch tail without hurting throughput.
Jordan: ran triangular jitter experiment: `--jitter-type=triangular --jitter-scale=0.6`. Results: kv_miss 6.0%, 95p=52ms. better but still above baseline.
Maria: trade-offs: lowering microbatch interval to 4ms should reduce KV churn but increases CPU overhead and slightly increases per-token cost (less batching). We need an SLO/cost trade table. Can someone produce quick numbers for throughput per-GPU with micro=4ms vs 8ms?
Lee: I'll run the throughput sweep on canary nodes: 15m windows at 4ms/8ms, jitter 0.2/1.0. Also will instrument `kernel_select_histogram` and `kv_eviction_rate` per-worker.
perf-bot: Scheduled job: perf/sweeps/micro_vs_jitter/ (canary pool). ETA 25m.
Jordan: action items: Maria — run cost delta calc for micro=4ms vs 8ms; Lee — run canary sweep and post kernel_select + kv metrics; I'll prepare a small patch to make fallback less eager (raise threshold for variant switch) and test in canary.
Maria: noted. I'll also prepare a short doc with expected unit cost impact (rough numbers: 4ms gives ~6% higher GPU token/sec cost but 95p latency down ~10%).
Lee: quick note — when you raise threshold for variant switch, make sure to cap the decision window so we don't keep a bad kernel forever for a changing sequence length distribution. add TTL to pinned variant.
Jordan: good call. I'll add TTL=30s in the patch.
Maria: ok, let's sync after canary completes. If canary shows kernel pin reduces tail without large cost change, we can roll a conservative change and keep micro=8ms for now. Otherwise we consider lowering microbatch_interval.
Lee: will post raw graphs (kernel select %, kv miss rate, 95/99 latencies) in this thread when done.
Jordan: thanks all — appreciate quick triage. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: Canary sweep started at 3577771220. Logs: https://perf.internal/runs/3577771220
Lee: posted canary graphs: https://perf.internal/runs/3577771220/graphs (kv_miss, kernel_select, latencies). Initial read: kernel pin reduces 95p by ~6ms, kv miss only slightly affected.
Maria: getting ready to present recommended rollback/mitigation in next infra sync.
Jordan: I'll open a short PR with kernel threshold change and TTL for canary testing: PR #4281
Lee: assigning follow-ups: PR review Jordan; canary metrics Lee; cost calc Maria. Let's reconvene in 90 minutes.
Maria: ack.
